quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #18
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When must you stop for a school bus?

options.text: When it is parked on the road shoulder and empty.
When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.
When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
Whenever the driver waves at you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
questions.explanation: You must stop when a school bus shows flashing red lights while picking up or dropping off children. On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop and stay stopped as long as the red lights are flashing or the stop arm is extended.

questions.question: What should car drivers know about large trucks?

options.text: They can stop faster than cars.
They need the same space to turn as cars.

questions.explanation: Large trucks have blind spots in front, on the sides, and in back. Stay out of these areas. Trucks also need more room to turn and stop than cars because of their size and weight.

questions.question: When a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light, who must yield?
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: When must drivers in Texas use their headlights?

options.text: When their vehicle has a mechanical problem.
From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
During the day in clear weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.
questions.explanation: Slow down when driving at night. Make sure you can stop within the distance your headlights shine. You must use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns of hazards that exist or may exist.
It alerts drivers to school zones.
It alerts drivers to recreation areas.
It alerts drivers to food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards that exist or may exist.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers about existing or possible hazards. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: Why should drivers be extra alert around motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?

options.text: They are hard to see in traffic.
They follow different traffic laws than larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are hard to see in traffic.
questions.explanation: In many crashes, drivers said they were looking but did not see the motorcycle, bicycle, or pedestrian. These are harder to spot because they are smaller, move faster, and have less noticeable lights. Always watch for these smaller road users to prevent collisions.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking their mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen when drivers go too fast for current conditions. Always drive at the legal speed limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: What must you do when a transit bus signals to rejoin traffic after stopping?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.explanation: You must yield to a transit bus that is signaling to return to the road after stopping to pick up or drop off passengers. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to let the bus safely enter traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a flagger is ahead controlling traffic in a construction area.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless:

options.text: You can clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle can go fast enough to pass.

questions.explanation: You cannot pass safely on a two-way, two-lane street unless you can see clearly ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic arrives, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Never pass where it is illegal or unsafe.

questions.question: If you are driving near a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
Let the motorcycle use only half of a lane.
Share the same lane with the motorcycle to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the motorcycle a full lane.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle is a full vehicle with the same road rights as any other vehicle. Give motorcyclists a full lane width. Even if there seems to be room for both vehicles in one lane, motorcycles need space to move safely.

questions.question: When the driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass safely and quickly.
questions.explanation: When a driver behind you wants to pass, slow down. This gives them enough space in front of your vehicle to complete the pass safely and in less time.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk to warn the bicyclist you are passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass.
Slow down and give as much space as possible.
Speed up and pull in front of the bicyclist quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down when passing a bicyclist and give them as much space as you can. Bicyclists have much less protection than drivers. Passing too quickly or too close can knock them off course.

questions.question: On long trips, you can prevent drowsiness by:

options.text: Moving your eyes side to side while driving.

questions.explanation: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop regularly to rest. Take time to stretch, even if you don't feel tired.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is a ____ line.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic lanes going in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the other lane is clear.

questions.question: Lack of sleep affects your driving ability the same way as:
questions.explanation: Fatigue and alcohol have similar effects on driving. Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving about as much as a blood alcohol level of 0.05%. Being awake for 24 hours straight affects driving the same way as a blood alcohol level of 0.10%.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped with lights flashing. You must:

options.text: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep the same speed.
Speed up to quickly pass the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and change lanes away from the vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: When you approach a stopped emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it extra space. If changing lanes is unsafe or there is only one lane, slow down below the speed limit and give the vehicle as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop at an emergency scene.

questions.question: You may drive in the HOV lane if:

options.text: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
You are driving faster than other traffic.
You need to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways reserve the left lane for vehicles with two or more people. These High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lanes are marked with signs and diamond symbols on the pavement.

questions.question: When you need to change lanes, it is important to:

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear before entering.

questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes or exiting a freeway, giving enough time to warn other drivers. Before moving left or right, turn your head and look over your shoulder to check that your blind spot is clear.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing. A parked car in this area can cause accidents.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your stopping ability. Slow down on poor roads. Wet and slippery roads require more distance to stop.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way at which traffic light?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.explanation: A red light means stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always insist on the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk
Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching
Enter a crosswalk anytime because the driver must stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you
Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder for traffic. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: This sign warns drivers about:

options.text: An upcoming curve in the road

questions.correctAnswerText: An upcoming curve in the road
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road curves to the right ahead.

questions.question: When it starts to sleet or snow, you should:

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear
Leave more distance between your vehicle and the cars ahead

questions.explanation: In snow and sleet, keep your windows and mirrors clear. Increase your distance behind other vehicles because slippery roads require more space to stop.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow other traffic instead of the guard
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic
Follow normal rules as if no children were present

questions.explanation: Always follow a crossing guard's directions. Slow down and use caution in school zones.

questions.question: If you need to slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?

options.text: Take your foot off the gas pedal

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal
questions.explanation: First, take your foot off the gas pedal. If you need to slow more, gently press the brake pedal with steady pressure.
